title: JEPA Atlas
scope: Technical briefs for the 19 papers added in the September review, not the complete awesome-JEPA catalog.
evidence_policy: 18 records have selected method/result sections checked; one is abstract-only. These are author-reported results, not independent replications. Schematic equations use normalized notation. Curator experiments are proposals, not paper claims. Publication acceptance is not inferred.

papers.name: CGM-JEPA
papers.title: CGM-JEPA: Learning Consistent Continuous Glucose Monitor Representations via Predictive Self-Supervised Pretraining
papers.problem: Learn useful glucose representations with scarce metabolic labels.
papers.intuition: Hide part of a glucose trace and predict its representation. A second view describes the distribution of glucose values, rather than their order.
papers.mechanism: CGM-JEPA predicts masked temporal embeddings; X-CGM-JEPA adds Glucodensity cross-view prediction. Evaluation freezes the encoder and fits a logistic classifier.
papers.objective: context glucose → predicted masked latent ≈ target latent; X-CGM adds cross-view alignment (schematic).
papers.training: Unlabeled CGM pretraining; labels used for downstream probes, not pretraining.
papers.deployment: CGM encoder plus fitted classifier; not an insulin policy.

results.protocol: Subject-level 2-fold CV repeated 20 times; small cohorts (N=27/17 in the study).
Same paper, endpoint-specific comparison.

limitations: Small-cohort phenotyping; no dosing or closed-loop safety experiment.
X-CGM does not win every metric or endpoint.
papers.experiment: For a new CGM study, split by subject before windowing; compare temporal-only versus temporal-plus-distribution embeddings with identical probes.

papers.name: GlucoFM
papers.title: GlucoFM: A Dual-Stream Foundation Model for Continuous Glucose Monitoring
papers.problem: Keep slow glucose state and short-lived events in the same representation.
papers.intuition: A daily baseline and a brief excursion tell different stories. Two streams try to retain both instead of averaging away the excursion.
papers.mechanism: Dual-stream latent modeling combines masked contextual reconstruction and temporal-dynamics constraints. The online encoder is retained; the EMA target branch is discarded.
papers.training: 477 subjects, 109,066 hours; compact 3-layer Transformers; 0.72M trainable parameters.
papers.deployment: Frozen 24-hour-window embeddings with a supervised downstream probe.

results.protocol: 10 repetitions of 5-fold subject-grouped CV; four downstream cohorts.
results.note: MantisV2 scores 64.7; heterogeneous pretraining is a separate comparison.

limitations: Not best on every endpoint; device/sampling shifts remain.
Metabolic classification does not establish safe insulin control.
papers.experiment: Probe slow-state and event streams separately. Test whether meal/exercise-related information survives compression, without labeling an observational association causal.

papers.name: TD-JEPA
papers.title: TD-JEPA: Latent-predictive Representations for Zero-Shot Reinforcement Learning
papers.problem: Learn task-adaptable control representations before rewards are specified.
papers.intuition: Instead of predicting only the next state, summarize what a policy will encounter over many future steps. Later, task weights select useful behavior.
papers.mechanism: Temporal-difference learning builds policy-conditioned multi-step latent predictions from reward-free offline transitions; the practical method uses symmetric objectives and orthonormality regularization.
papers.objective: T(φ(s),a,z) ≈ stopgrad[ψ(s′) + γ T(φ(s′),a′,z)], a′ ~ π_z (normalized Eq. 9).
papers.training: Offline state/action/next-state transitions; target networks and task-conditioned policies.
papers.deployment: Infer a task representation and use its policy without task-specific policy retraining.

results.protocol: Paper-matched visual-control evaluation; not a success rate.

limitations: Idealized theoretical assumptions and learned feature/task coverage matter.
Not an arbitrary-reward or safety guarantee.
papers.experiment: Hold the offline dataset fixed; test unseen reward functions and identify which lie outside the representation’s task span.
papers.audit: This arXiv ID is the zero-shot-RL TD-JEPA. The similarly named baseline in D-JEPA is a different work; no identity or citation edge is inferred.

papers.name: XP-JEPA
papers.title: XP-JEPA: Cross-Predictive Physics Grounding for Forecastable Latent Dynamics
papers.problem: An easy-to-predict latent space may still miss physical distinctions needed for control.
papers.intuition: Two scenes can look alike but react differently to the same action. Training-time physical trajectories provide a second account of what really changes.
papers.mechanism: Separate visual/physical encoders share an action-conditioned predictor. Each branch predicts both future modalities; per-branch regularization discourages collapse.
papers.objective: L ≈ Σ_{m,n∈{vision,state}} ||g(z_t^m,a_t) − z_{t+1}^n||² + β(Ω_vision + Ω_state) (Eq. 1, abbreviated).
papers.training: Paired visual observations, actions and privileged physical trajectories.
papers.deployment: Discard the physical branch; visual-only latent planning.

results.protocol: Matched data/planner; three seeds.
Original predictor removed and an identical fresh predictor fitted.

limitations: Physical-state decodability alone does not imply forecastability.
Visual robotics results are not physiological-control validation.
papers.experiment: Compare privileged-state regression against cross-prediction; then freeze both encoders and refit the same predictor to separate representation gains from co-adaptation.
papers.audit: Earlier curation called this JEPA-x. The inspected v1 article uses XP-JEPA; the arXiv ID is unchanged.

papers.name: Delta-JEPA
papers.title: Delta-JEPA: Learning Action-Sensitive World Models via Latent Difference Decoding
papers.problem: Latent predictions can be insensitive to the action that caused a transition.
papers.intuition: Make the change between two embeddings reveal which action occurred. This discourages a representation that ignores the control input.
papers.mechanism: An auxiliary decoder reconstructs actions from consecutive latent differences alongside forward latent prediction.
papers.objective: L = L_prediction + λ L_action; â_t = decoder(z_{t+1} − z_t) (Eq. 7, schematic decoder).
papers.deployment: Use the learned action-conditioned world model for planning.

results.protocol: Paper’s visual continuous-control evaluation.
results.uncertainty: Reported ±1.90 versus ±1.50; uncertainty convention not extracted.

results.protocol: Same evaluation table.
results.uncertainty: Reported ±1.81 versus ±1.89; uncertainty convention not extracted.

limitations: Four visual tasks; one-step action recovery need not capture delayed effects.
Action-sensitive features need not contain every exogenous task-relevant variable.
papers.experiment: Use matched transitions to test action recovery at several lags. Separately test retention of exogenous variables needed for the reward.

papers.name: D-JEPA
papers.title: D-JEPA: A Decision-Aligned Latent World Model
papers.problem: Accurate-looking future embeddings may rank candidate actions incorrectly.
papers.intuition: A planner needs the best candidate, not just a plausible forecast. Outcome feedback can teach a small correction to the ranking.
papers.mechanism: Bounded, permutation-equivariant corrections use goal-relative candidate descriptors and executed-outcome supervision. Successful candidates receive probability mass while trust/locality terms constrain corrections.
papers.objective: L ≈ −log Σ_{i:success} softmax(−s/T)_i + λ_local L_local + λ_trust mean(δ²) (Eq. 2).
papers.training: Candidate futures plus realized outcome labels; not reward-free pretraining.
papers.deployment: Calibrate candidate scores before selecting an action.

results.protocol: 256 evaluation cases; LeWM also scores 83.59.
100 cases in this separate evaluation.

limitations: Empirical ranking improvements are not safety certificates.
Different from denoising D-JEPA (2410.03755).
papers.experiment: Construct a fixed candidate pool; measure realized regret and ranking correlation, not only latent MSE. Hold the candidate generator constant.
papers.audit: Denoising D-JEPA and decision-aligned D-JEPA are separate papers. The TD-JEPA baseline named in this paper is not automatically the zero-shot-RL TD-JEPA in this atlas.

papers.name: Exogenous-feature study
papers.title: Predictive Objectives Discard Exogenous Control-Relevant Features: A Controlled Mechanistic Study
aliases: Predictive Objectives Discard Exogenous Control-Relevant Features

locators: Main controlled study; Figure 4; Appendix Table 4

papers.problem: Predictability or controllability may select the wrong information for a future task.
papers.intuition: A variable can matter to your decision even when your action cannot change it. “Useful for prediction” and “useful for control” are different tests.
papers.mechanism: Controlled experiments cross controllability with task relevance, holding architecture/data comparable across predictive and task-grounded objectives.
papers.objective: Diagnostic: probe each controllability × relevance quadrant; vary reward supervision rather than assuming predictive loss is sufficient.
papers.training: Synthetic controlled environments; reward-free versus partially reward-grounded objectives.
papers.deployment: An analysis/diagnostic, not a deployable controller.

results.protocol: 2% versus 1% reward grounding; diagnostic threshold 0.75.
results.note: Reward-free conditions are near chance in the studied setup.

limitations: Deliberately narrow mechanistic construction, not a universal JEPA theorem.
Reward grounding is not shown to solve all feature-selection failures.
papers.experiment: Create a controlled driver-blindness test: vary whether a driver is predictable, controllable and reward-relevant independently. Evaluate each factor with a probe.

papers.name: Semigroup-JEPA
papers.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
papers.problem: One-step accuracy may not survive recursive rollout under changed physics.
papers.intuition: An error becomes the next input. Training through several predicted steps exposes that feedback rather than hiding it with the true next state.
papers.mechanism: Gravity-conditioned encoder/predictor training uses recursive latent rollout and SIGReg. Fresh-predictor tests distinguish representation gains from the original predictor.
papers.training: Narrow gravity distributions; history H=20; GRU/SSM variants.
papers.deployment: Supplied gravity remains an input. Control uses separately trained diffusion policies on frozen features.

results.task: 2D square: fresh GRU on frozen encoders
results.protocol: Same newly fitted GRU; GRU-trained encoder versus Transformer-trained encoder.

limitations: Unknown physical parameters are not inferred.
Theory uses linear features; nonlinear/contact behavior has additional caveats.
papers.experiment: Report teacher-forced and free-rollout error separately, then replace the predictor. Test supplied-parameter errors before claiming adaptation.

papers.name: RD-JEPA
papers.title: RD-JEPA: Predictive latent pretraining for few-trajectory transfer across reaction–diffusion equations
papers.problem: Forecast a new reaction law using very few target trajectories.
papers.intuition: Learn common dynamical features from related systems, then spend the small adaptation budget on the unfamiliar system instead of learning everything again.
papers.mechanism: Predictive-latent pretraining transfers to supervised full-field forecasting; three held-out reaction families are excluded from pretraining.
papers.objective: Source predictive-latent pretraining → target-system adaptation → field forecasts (pipeline, not a transcribed loss).
papers.training: Five source equation families; unseen-system adaptation with 1, 5 or 10 trajectories.
papers.deployment: Adapted forecaster receives observed fields and the forecast horizon.

results.protocol: Horizon average h=1…5; same 300 test trajectories; three paired support selections.
results.note: Multiply table values by 0.01 for the unscaled relative error.

limitations: Related PDE families and finite horizons, not universal physics transfer.
Only three paired support selections; no formal hypothesis test reported.
papers.experiment: Separate source-system reuse from genuinely held-out dynamics. Use identical support trajectories and a strong non-JEPA pretrained baseline.

papers.name: Phys-JEPA
papers.title: Phys-JEPA: Physics-Informed Latent World Models for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

locators: Eqs. 6–12; Tables 2–5; compact robustness check Table 8

papers.problem: Keep known physical descriptors and their changes meaningful in a learned forecaster.
papers.intuition: Give part of the embedding a job you can inspect; let the remaining part model what those descriptors do not explain.
papers.mechanism: Splits physical/residual latents; combines decoded forecasting, latent prediction, physical-state consistency and physical-change consistency.
papers.objective: L = L_forecast + αL_JEPA + βL_reg + λ_sL_state + λ_dL_dynamics (Eq. 12).
papers.training: Observed sequences and selected physical descriptors; moment regularization on residual features.
papers.deployment: Encode a history, forecast latents, decode the future sequence.

results.protocol: L=96; main single-seed setting; aggregate over variables.
L=96; main single-seed setting; aggregate over variables.

limitations: Main tables are single-seed; compact two-seed checks do not reproduce the full model’s Traffic advantage.
Hybrid supervision; short-horizon Electricity is worse than the supervised baseline.
papers.experiment: Ablate state consistency and change consistency separately. Compare actual physical measurements with engineered descriptive statistics.
papers.audit: Its Eq. 11 labels a mean/covariance moment penalty SIGReg. Do not assume this is identical to a characteristic-function SIGReg implementation merely because the name matches.

papers.name: Eidos
papers.title: EIDOS: Latent-Space Predictive Learning for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.problem: Combine useful latent predictability with accurate observable forecasts.
papers.intuition: A compact latent space still needs an anchor to what will be measured. Test whether representation alignment adds anything beyond the forecast loss.
papers.mechanism: Causal Transformer learning combines latent alignment, observation grounding and direct forecasting supervision.
papers.objective: L = L_forecast + λ_align L_latent + λ_ground L_observation (schematic decomposition).
papers.training: Historical and future time-series observations; hybrid objectives.
papers.deployment: Time-series forecasting, not latent-space action search.

results.protocol: Same-paper objective ablation; latent-only variant is 0.5570.
Latent-only also 0.7678: alignment alone is not the full gain.

limitations: Hybrid supervision must be preserved in fair comparisons.
Aggregate gains do not prove every dataset or horizon improves.
papers.experiment: Use a 2×2 ablation of latent alignment and observation grounding at fixed capacity, data and training budget.

papers.name: LeNEPA
papers.title: LeNEPA: No-Augmentation Next-Latent Prediction for Time-Series Representation Learning
papers.problem: Reuse a time-series pretraining recipe without hand-designed augmentations.
papers.intuition: Predict the next latent token and prevent the whole space collapsing. Then check whether the same recipe works on a different signal family.
papers.mechanism: Causal next-latent prediction with SIGReg; no EMA or stop-gradient. Separate pretraining runs reuse one fixed recipe.
papers.objective: L ≈ next-latent cosine prediction + λ SIGReg(z) (schematic).
papers.deployment: Frozen representation probes; recipe transfer is not shared-checkpoint zero-shot transfer.

results.protocol: Median across five seeds; fixed L4 LeNEPA readout versus best-layer JEPA.
CauKer pretraining; frozen embeddings plus Random Forest; best LeNEPA checkpoint.

limitations: Readout selection differs in the reported table.
Not a claim of superiority to optimally retuned baselines; UCR score is below Mantis.
papers.experiment: Pre-register the readout layer and checkpoint rule. Separate recipe robustness from frozen-checkpoint transfer.

papers.name: Distributed JEPA
papers.title: Distributed JEPA: A Self-Supervised Framework for Energy Forecasting
papers.problem: Transfer energy forecasting representations between heterogeneous assets.
papers.intuition: Try to share temporal structure without requiring every solar installation or building to have identical data.
papers.mechanism: Masked temporal embedding prediction with covariance and temporal-variance regularization; evaluates asset transfer and degraded data.
papers.objective: Masked latent prediction + covariance/temporal-variance regularization; exact loss not extracted.
papers.training: Heterogeneous energy time series; full training protocol not checked.
papers.deployment: Asset-level forecasting; deployment inputs not fully extracted.

results.protocol: Abstract reports improvement on 9/10 assets; horizons, splits and seeds not extracted.

limitations: Abstract-only record: numerical range is author-reported, not table-audited.
Not a comprehensive forecasting leaderboard.
papers.experiment: Before reuse, extract the test-asset split, missingness process, horizons and scaling rules; compare per asset, not only the aggregate.

papers.name: FF-JEPA
papers.title: FF-JEPA: Long-Horizon Planning in World Models with Latent Planners
papers.problem: Long-horizon search needs useful intermediate targets without a supplied goal image.
papers.intuition: First propose where to go next in latent space; then use a short-horizon action planner to get there.
papers.mechanism: An action-free latent subgoal planner complements an action-conditioned forward model. Diffusion and deterministic planners are studied; action search uses CEM.
papers.objective: G(history) → subgoal; CEM minimizes predicted distance to that subgoal (planning schematic).
papers.training: Behavior trajectories for world-model and latent-planner learning.
papers.deployment: Learned subgoals plus receding-horizon search; no explicit goal image.

results.protocol: 256 evaluation episodes under the paper’s long-initialization protocol.
Same paper; far smaller short-horizon gap.

limitations: Preliminary single-environment evidence.
Some external baselines in the table use different protocols.
papers.experiment: Compare learned subgoals to random, expert and interpolated subgoals under equal environment interaction and action-search budgets.
papers.audit: The random-initialization success differs between Table I (82.42) and prose (82.25). It is excluded from the numerical records pending reconciliation.

papers.name: SkyJEPA
papers.title: SkyJEPA: Learning Long-Horizon World Models for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Control of Quadrotors
papers.problem: Control a real quadrotor using latent dynamics trained in simulation.
papers.intuition: Imagine motion in a compressed space, then translate it back into physical states so a controller can evaluate trajectory costs.
papers.mechanism: Encodes histories of estimated full states and motor actions, rolls latent dynamics forward, and uses a physics-inspired state prober inside MPPI.
papers.objective: state/action history → latent rollout → physical-state probe → MPPI cost (pipeline).
papers.training: Domain-randomized simulation; state histories include pose, velocities and attitude.
papers.deployment: Estimated full-state observations and action history; not vision-only control.

results.protocol: Real closed-loop tracking in the paper’s flight setup.
Physics-inspired versus generic prober within JEPA.

limitations: Platform-specific sim-to-real results, not formal robust-control guarantees.
Separate prober improvements from representation improvements.
papers.experiment: Ablate the prober while keeping latent dynamics fixed; record latency, model error and closed-loop cost under the same disturbances.

papers.name: WA-JEPA
papers.title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving
papers.problem: Couple future-scene prediction and action generation without averaging away uncertain futures.
papers.intuition: Generate possible latent futures jointly with actions, rather than forcing all plausible futures into one mean representation.
papers.mechanism: Future-masked video pretraining followed by joint future/action modeling with conditional flow matching.
papers.objective: Past video → future latents and actions; conditional flow-matching objective (schematic, not deterministic latent regression).
papers.training: nuPlan video pretraining; NAVSIM navtrain action/world training.
papers.deployment: Multi-view video history with joint future–action generation.

results.protocol: Different backbones; stochastic evaluations use 10 seeds.
results.note: EPDMS* 88.0 is the pre-correction aggregation; do not mix columns.

limitations: Driving-specific evaluation and substantial compute.
Stochastic predictions are not automatically calibrated risk estimates.
papers.experiment: At fixed inference budget compare deterministic regression with sampled latent futures; assess calibration and candidate diversity separately.

papers.name: JEPA-Anything
papers.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
papers.problem: A single undifferentiated target can entangle different predictive factors.
papers.intuition: Give several subspaces different parts of the prediction job; reconstruct a shared predicted state from their outputs.
papers.mechanism: Learned projectors split a stopped-gradient target into K orthogonality-regularized factors. Factor predictors and state synthesis augment domain-specific base losses.
papers.objective: z_k = P_kᵀ stopgrad(z); L = L_base + L_factor-pred + regularizers (Eqs. 3–10, abbreviated).
papers.training: Domain-specific tokenizers/backbones; EMA target encoder; factor projectors remain trainable.
papers.deployment: Online features or synthesized future states feed task-specific readouts/planners.

results.protocol: Same learned-grid readout and matched pretraining; ten seeds.
Matched readout, not the supplied-grid setting.

limitations: Shared objective is not a single cross-domain pretrained model.
Orthogonal factors do not automatically identify causal variables.
papers.experiment: Hold latent dimension and parameter count fixed; compare one predictor, multiple unconstrained heads and orthogonally regularized heads.

papers.name: Clin-JEPA intervention study
papers.title: Intervention Granularity Matters: Coherent Treatment Bundles in Counterfactual Simulation with Clinical World Models
papers.problem: Counterfactual edits may leave the support of clinically coherent treatment combinations.
papers.intuition: Changing one setting while freezing all related settings can describe an implausible intervention. Compare coherent bundles instead.
papers.mechanism: A frozen clinical world model compares isolated component edits with co-occurring ventilation-treatment bundles, including equal-edit-magnitude controls.
papers.objective: Compare Δz_next(bundle) against Δz_next(single edit), controlling perturbation magnitude (diagnostic, not a causal estimator).
papers.training: MIMIC-IV patient trajectories; frozen Clin-JEPA used for the intervention audit.
papers.deployment: Counterfactual latent-response analysis only; no treatment-policy deployment.

results.protocol: 1,019 of 1,089 targets; next-hour analysis.
Model-response association; 5,000 bootstrap resamples.

limitations: Predicted response is not an identified treatment effect.
No clinical benefit or safe intervention policy established.
papers.experiment: For any action-conditioned model, define the valid joint intervention set before querying counterfactuals; flag extrapolated combinations.

papers.name: VL-JEPA
papers.title: VL-JEPA: Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Vision-language
papers.problem: Predict semantic answers without generating text tokens at every instant.
papers.intuition: Update what the model means continuously; translate that meaning into words only when a readout is needed.
papers.mechanism: Vision plus a text query predicts the target-text embedding. A separate lightweight decoder produces language selectively.
papers.objective: L = D(predicted text embedding, target text embedding); decode only on selected steps.
papers.training: Embedding prediction pretraining followed by VQA supervised fine-tuning.
papers.deployment: Embedding-based retrieval/classification; optional selective text decoding.

results.protocol: Similar average CIDEr; approximately 2.85× fewer decoding operations.
results.note: Operation count reduction, not an end-to-end latency speedup.

limitations: 1.6B-parameter model; efficiency comparison depends on matched setup.
Selection benchmark does not establish causally online event detection in every setting.
papers.experiment: Measure semantic update rate and decoder calls separately. Benchmark total latency and whether a causal trigger matches offline selection.

concepts.name: Predict representations
concepts.question: What should be predicted?
concepts.plain: An encoder compresses observations into z. A predictor learns a target representation rather than every raw measurement.
concepts.technical: Distinguish masked reconstruction in representation space, next-step prediction and policy-conditioned multi-step prediction. They impose different information requirements.
concepts.caution: Low latent loss alone does not show that the state contains everything a task needs.

concepts.name: Prevent collapse
concepts.question: Why not output one constant?
concepts.plain: If both sides learn the same constant, prediction is trivial and the representation is useless.
concepts.technical: Record the actual regularizer, target update and gradient path. EMA, stop-gradient, moment penalties and distribution matching are not interchangeable recipes.
concepts.caution: A shared acronym is not evidence of an identical loss.

concepts.name: Retain action effects
concepts.question: Does changing an action change the right future?
concepts.plain: A controller needs a model that distinguishes what its candidate actions do.
concepts.technical: Test forward sensitivity, inverse action recovery and delayed responses separately.
concepts.caution: Controllability is not the same as task relevance.

concepts.name: Align decisions
concepts.question: Does the best predicted candidate really work best?
concepts.plain: Good forecasts are useful only if the decision rule can use them.
concepts.technical: Compare predicted candidate ranks with executed costs; measure regret at a fixed candidate pool and search budget.
concepts.caution: A ranking improvement is not a safety guarantee.

concepts.name: Control rollout error
concepts.question: What happens after repeated prediction?
concepts.plain: A small prediction error changes the next input and can grow over multiple steps.
concepts.technical: Separate teacher-forced one-step error from free rollout; replace the predictor to test what the encoder learned.
concepts.caution: A multi-step training loss alone does not certify stability.

concepts.name: Ground the latent state
concepts.question: Which observable or physical quantities anchor z?
concepts.plain: A useful latent space can be tied to measurements, physical states or descriptors.
concepts.technical: Distinguish training-only privileged data from quantities required at deployment, and state decoding from transition consistency.
concepts.caution: A decodable state is not necessarily a forecastable state.

concepts.name: Keep external drivers
concepts.question: What matters even though the agent cannot control it?
concepts.plain: Some outside signals matter for outcomes without responding to the agent’s actions.
concepts.technical: Probe task relevance independently of controllability; define support before interpreting counterfactual model responses.
concepts.caution: An observational association is not a causal intervention effect.

concepts.name: Read time-series structure
concepts.question: Which timescales and subjects are represented?
concepts.plain: Slow state, brief events, sampling rate and subject identity can all change what an embedding means.
concepts.technical: Use subject/system-disjoint splits, explicit horizons and matched downstream probes; distinguish recipe reuse from checkpoint transfer.
concepts.caution: A glucose classifier is not an insulin controller.

concepts.name: Factorize predictions
concepts.question: Should different latent subspaces have different jobs?
concepts.plain: Split a predictive target into complementary parts rather than one unrestricted vector.
concepts.technical: Control latent width, number of heads and regularization when testing a factorized target.
concepts.caution: Orthogonality does not prove semantic or causal disentanglement.

concepts.name: Represent multiple futures
concepts.question: Is one predicted future enough?
concepts.plain: A deterministic mean may hide several plausible outcomes.
concepts.technical: Conditional generative latent models require separate calibration and coverage tests before risk-sensitive use.
concepts.caution: Diversity is not a calibrated probability distribution.

paths.name: From representation to control
paths.description: Separate action sensitivity, forecastability and decision quality.
steps: Ask whether the embedding reacts to actions.
Test whether physical grounding improves new-predictor forecasts.
Check candidate ordering against real outcomes.
Audit the information these objectives may discard.

paths.name: Glucose and time series
paths.description: Read representation quality without confusing it with therapy.
steps: Begin with masked and cross-view CGM embeddings.
Separate slow state from transient events.
Test the need for observation grounding.
Distinguish recipe portability from frozen transfer.
Audit counterfactual support before interpreting actions.

paths.name: Changing dynamics
paths.description: Compare three very different meanings of adaptation.
steps: Use physical state only while training.
Supply a changing parameter at prediction time.
Finetune on a few trajectories from a new law.

paths.name: Planning and possible futures
paths.description: Follow subgoals, stochastic futures and latent factors.
steps: Learn subgoals to shorten action search.
Model uncertain futures jointly with actions.
Study factorized prediction and its assumptions.
Decouple semantic prediction from expensive readout.

relations.why: GlucoFM re-trains CGM-JEPA and X-CGM-JEPA on the same corpus.
Compare training-only physical grounding against a supplied deployment-time physics parameter.
Action sensitivity and retention of exogenous task-relevant information are separate requirements; no head-to-head experiment is claimed.
Candidate ranking and fresh-predictor forecastability evaluate different failure modes.
Both use observational grounding, but Phys-JEPA adds explicit physical/residual structure.
Diffusion subgoals and flow-matched joint futures/actions have different roles in planning.
Few-trajectory finetuning on a new equation differs from parameter-conditioned zero-shot generalization.
